prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1462; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Insured reported a sideswipe during a lane change. The insured's policy is active and the driver listed on the policy is the person who was operating the vehicle at the time.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained an attorney, who has asked that all communication go through their office. Claimant's account of the collision has remained the same in every conversation so far.

Entry 3: Photos submitted with the file confirm several details of the contact point and the vehicle positions. There are no independent witnesses to the lane change itself.

Entry 4: Damage to both vehicles is mostly consistent with the described impact. A few older scratches near the rear quarter panel may predate this loss and have been noted separately.

Entry 5: Responding officer's report and statements from witnesses indicate the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred. This conflicts with the claimant's own description and needs to be reconciled before any payment decision.

Entry 6: Claimant reports a back strain from the collision. Medical records show a treatment course that ran somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury, and no prior injury to the same area has come up in the records reviewed so far.

Entry 7: The impact appears to have been very light, which makes the severity of the claimed injury difficult to match to the physical damage. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage start date.

Entry 8: Referred the file to the claims review group for a second look at the injury causation and the conflicting statements about the claimant's location. Attorney has been notified that the claim is under further review and that a decision will follow once that review is complete.
